Recommended before push: reword the commit/PR to 'Refs #6681' and 'partial mitigation, TSan leg not re-run'; record the last error inside the helper (see up-1b); optionally replace the retry with settle_key_claims on both keys then ONE strict attach. trigger: a future reader trusts the comment that says a filler thread can still be racing toward arm_park.mu when spin_until returns

The wait is now `arm_park.parked == kFillerCount` read under arm_park.mu, so all four fillers have already passed maybe_park's locked read; the sentence is false. The lock_guard around `park_every = 0` stays correct and required by BlockingGate's own contract (lines 112-115), not by a filler race. Raised independently by security-guardian (sec-2) and docs-writer (doc-1) in the same Gate 2 wave; cpp-expert (ce-2) and cpp-safety (cs-1) concur as downstream echoes; truth owner cpp-safety/cpp-expert. classification_rationale: dead variable plus an uncommented (void) cast; wording/cleanliness, no behaviour
summary: `const int base_entries = b->arm_entries.load();` (11003) is now only silenced by `(void)base_entries;` (11034); grep finds no other use (requester question (c): yes, dead). trigger: a maintainer edits a wait on the authority of the helper comment (e.g. waits on disarm_entries, which is earlier and worse)
classification_rationale: ordinary C++ comment contradicts the FakeBackend code and the file's own declaration comment; not adjacent to a control branch
summary: The helper comment, the commit message and the #6681 issue comment say FakeBackend::disarms is bumped at disarm() ENTRY. FALSE (orchestrator verified at test lines ~272-291): disarm_entries is bumped at entry; `disarms.fetch_add(1)` is the LAST statement of disarm(), after disarm_park.maybe_park(lane). The file's FakeBackend declaration comment (~192-199) and the settle_key_claims comment (~8010-8012) state it correctly. The race itself is real - the runtime's completion continuation (publish verdicts, pop the claim FIFO, runtime ~1343-1356) runs AFTER backend disarm() returns - so the fix is sound; only the stated mechanism is wrong. Raised independently by cpp-expert (ce-1) and quality-engineer (qe-2) in the Gate 3 wave; consistency-auditor (c-1) and compliance-officer (comp-2) are downstream echoes. Recommended: fold - reword to 'disarms is bumped when the backend disarm() returns, before the compensating-disarm continuation pops the claims from their FIFO'.

trigger: a maintainer reuses attach_past_wedge_refusal for an EXISTING rule id and the second refusal site (runtime ~3442) fires after detach_rule_locked
classification_rationale: ordinary C++ comment slightly false in general; harmless at the three brand-new-id call sites
summary: Helper comment says 'A refusal mutates nothing'. Both refusal sites bump wedged_refusals_ (relaxed; runtime 3169, 3442); the second site (3436-3446) fires AFTER detach_rule_locked(rule_id) and returns prior_state_preserved=false, so a refusal there DOES mutate an existing rule (consistency-auditor c-3 extension). The first (hoisted, 3165-3175) site returns before detach_rule_locked/index_->add/claim creation, and 'r-fresh' is a brand-new id, so the retry is observably side-effect free at all three call sites; wedged_refusals reads (11122, 11609, 11671, 11823, 11882, 11916, 11980) are outside the three modified TEST_CASEs. Raised by security-guardian (sec-3); ce-5, cs-3 and c-3 are downstream echoes. Recommended: fold - 'a refusal of a brand-new rule id mutates no rule state (only the wedged_refusals_ counter)'.

trigger: attach_past_wedge_refusal's REQUIRE(spin_until) throws inside the helper (runtime keeps refusing or arm times out), so the call-site CAPTURE never executes
classification_rationale: absence of diagnostics, not a contradiction
summary: On a timeout Catch2 prints only `REQUIRE( spin_until(...) )` with false; the last error string is lost, defeating the CAPTURE added at each site. A permanently wedged runtime DOES still fail loudly at 10 s x kSpinScale (6 on TSan/ASan = 60 s) - the helper cannot mask it (requester question (a): confirmed). Raised independently by cpp-expert (ce-4) and quality-engineer (qe-3, which also notes it) in the Gate 3 wave. Recommended: fold - take the spin_until result into a bool, CAPTURE the last error, then REQUIRE; or INFO the error inside the helper before the REQUIRE.

trigger: a runtime regression delays retirement of the retained wedge by less than 10 s x kSpinScale (tolerated, where the old test failed on any lag), or a maintainer sees two idioms for one race class
classification_rationale: an exact quiescence signal already exists in the file and was not used; not a contradiction
summary: The file's established idiom for this race is settle_key_claims (8013, anonymous namespace; claim_queue_depth_for_test(key)==0 then active_backend_op_workers()==0; used at 8065, 8078, 8135, 8151, 8201, 8211, 8259, 8305, 8348; raw depth==0 spins at 4072, 6407 (both keys), 6473, 6565). The retry-past-refusal helper is a second idiom and tolerates up to 10 s x scale of slow retirement; it also does NOT cover the 'arm timed out' shape (see up-1). Waiting on queue depth for both keys then ONE strict attach is exact, keeps the original strictness and removes the up-1 window. Raised by quality-engineer (qe-3) and consistency-auditor (c-2, shown qe-3) and chaos-injector (CH-1 remedy). Not required to merge. Recommended: fold (small) or file.

trigger: a legitimate future runtime change compensates (rather than adopts) late successes of abandoned filler claims, so rule_count() never reaches before+4
classification_rationale: undocumented test dependency on adoption semantics; not a contradiction
summary: The new `rule_count() >= rules_before_fillers + kFillerCount` wait asserts each filler's late success is ADOPTED (CallbackAdopt / wedge_may_adopt, runtime ~1556-1654). Holds today: cpp-safety verified by code read that the conditions hold for the 4 distinct rule ids/keys, and happy-path/quality-engineer observed exactly +4 over hundreds of runs. If it ever failed it would fail LOUDLY after 10 s x scale (a correct loud failure, with a bare spin_until timeout message). Recommended: a comment naming the adoption dependency.

trigger: a detached filler worker is still in its post-commit tail (completion-object destructor, executor bookkeeping, thread exit) when main() returns
classification_rationale: absence of a stronger quiescence wait; residual of the exit-crash class, not a contradiction

Raised by security-guardian (sec-1); quality-engineer (qe-4, LOW, likely) and cpp-safety (cs-4, rated speculative with I5/I9 reading) are downstream echoes. cpp-safety found no reachable crash it can name in that tail; adding the wait is optional hardening (bounded, non-throwing). Segfault candidate mechanisms (none proven): (1) detached worker logging via spdlog after main returns - closed for these 4 workers by the diff; (2) thread-exit tail - not closed; (3) other tests with the same shape - not touched; (4) backend/runtime destroyed under a worker - unlikely (shared_ptr). Recommended: file with the exit-crash class follow-up, or fold the active_total wait.

trigger: Catch2 default order is rand with a time seed, so a test whose detached/parked workers commit and log after the test case can be the LAST test in a shard process and race main()'s return

SPECULATIVE: the exit-segfault cause was never backtraced (gdb and an LD_PRELOAD shim masked the timing); evidence is log ordering ('Session::run() returned 0 (main about to return)' then 'arm committed for rule f0...') plus the symptom disappearing locally. Derived MEDIUM so it does not gate; recorded as a mandatory-investigation candidate (chaos CH-4: loop each hang-idiom test last under --rng-seed, 500x each). Operator decision needed: file a follow-up (disposition left open; no issue filed by this run).
